task: Redesign The Bayes Group website (apps/bayes-group-site) so it looks like a well-established, premium consulting firm and is clearly positioned for small and medium-sized businesses first, with enterprise clients served at a premium level. Make it far more graphic and visually rich: professional photography, custom illustrations and icons, confident typography and layered sections, instead of today's plain text-and-card pages. Keep the stack and everything the site already does: Vite + React + TypeScript + react-router, plain CSS with the design-token theme, system fonts only, every page prerendered to its own HTML file with its own title, meta description, Open Graph tags and canonical link, the hydrated training filter, Menu button and contact form, and no backend, analytics, third-party scripts or external CDNs. Existing acceptance tests keep passing except where this task changes that behavior (listed below). Brand: deep navy #0B1F3A, white, and teal #1F8A8A as the one accent; tints and shades of these are fine (e.g. a darker navy for premium bands, a pale teal-grey for alternate section backgrounds). Serif headings, sans-serif body, larger and more confident than now: a display size for the hero h1 (about 56-64px on desktop, 36-40px on phones), generous spacing, a consistent 8px spacing scale, cards with soft shadows that lift slightly on hover. Subtle motion only (fade/slide-in of sections, hover lifts), all of it turned off under prefers-reduced-motion. WCAG AA contrast everywhere, including text over photos. Photography (already in the app, do not generate or download images): public/images/ holds eight photos, each as NAME.jpg (1344x768) and NAME-768.jpg (768x439): hero-boardroom, smb-owner, team-workshop, enterprise-atrium, custom-development, strategy-session, about-office, contact-meeting. Use them with (or ) with srcset (768w and 1344w), sizes, width and height attributes, loading="lazy" except the hero, decoding="async", and descriptive alt text (e.g. "Meeting room with a wall screen showing data visualizations"); they are scene photos, never captioned or presented as the firm's own team or clients. Where text sits on a photo, put a navy gradient overlay behind it so the text meets WCAG AA. Illustrations: draw them as inline SVG in the brand colors (no image files): a line icon for every service item, training format and engagement tier, drawn in one consistent style (24px grid, 1.5-2px strokes); a subtle background motif of overlapping bell curves or a fine data-grid pattern behind the hero and the dark bands; numbered step markers joined by a line in "How we work". Navigation: header nav links become Services, Training, Engagements, About, Contact, plus the "Book a consultation" button; the footer nav lists the same five links. The header is sticky, white with a hairline bottom border once the page scrolls; on phones the links collapse into the "Menu" button as now. Pages: 1. Home (/): keep the h1 "Evidence-driven AI, built for your business." and change the value proposition to "We help small and medium-sized businesses put AI to work, with enterprise-grade rigor and senior data scientists on every engagement." Sections in order: - Hero: full-width hero-boardroom photo with the navy gradient overlay and the bell-curve motif, the h1, the value proposition, and the "Book a consultation" (to /contact) and "Explore services" (to /services) buttons. - Credibility strip right under the hero: four short points with icons: "Credentialed data scientists", "Vendor-neutral advice", "Built for small and medium-sized businesses", "Enterprise-grade governance". No numbers, client names or logos. - Who we serve: two side-by-side panels (stacked on phones). "Small and medium-sized businesses" is the larger, primary panel with the smb-owner photo, two sentences about practical, right-sized AI with fast results and a team that owns it afterwards, and a link "See engagements" to /engagements. "Enterprise" is the premium panel on dark navy with the enterprise-atrium photo, two sentences about a dedicated senior team, custom scope and governance for larger organizations, a "Premium" label, and a link "Enterprise engagements" to /engagements#enterprise. - The three pillar cards as now ("AI Enablement", "Training", "Custom Development", each with "Learn more" to /services#enablement, /services#training, /services#custom-development), each with its icon and a photo strip on top (strategy-session, team-workshop, custom-development). - "How we work" with the four numbered steps Assess, Design, Build, Enable as now, joined by a line on desktop. - Case studies: heading "Client results", three case-study cards, each with an industry ("Manufacturing", "Professional services", "Retail"), a challenge, our approach and a result line, every card visibly marked with a "Placeholder" tag and the note "Placeholder case study: replace with a real client engagement before launch." Invent no client names and no numbers; the result line says "Result: to be added from a real engagement." - One testimonial block on navy, marked "Placeholder testimonial: replace with a real client quote before launch.", attributed to "Client name, Title, Company". - "Why The Bayes Group" with its four points as now, beside the about-office photo. - The call-to-action band "Ready to put AI to work?" with the "Book a consultation" button, on navy with the bell-curve motif. 2. Engagements (/engagements, new page; title "Engagements | The Bayes Group", h1 "Engagements"): an intro sentence ("Right-sized engagements for small and medium-sized businesses, and a premium tier for enterprise."), then four tier cards in this order, no prices anywhere: - "Jumpstart" (for small and medium-sized businesses; typical timeline "2 to 4 weeks"): AI readiness assessment, top three use cases prioritized, one quick-win prototype, a 90-day roadmap. - "Build" (for small and medium-sized businesses; "6 to 12 weeks"): one custom AI solution designed, built and deployed, integration with your existing systems, team training, handover documentation. - "Partner" (for small and medium-sized businesses; "Ongoing, monthly"): a senior data scientist on call, monthly improvement sprints, model monitoring and updates, quarterly roadmap reviews. - "Enterprise" (section id "enterprise"; "Premium" label; "Custom scope"): a dedicated senior team, multi-team programs and centers of excellence, AI governance and responsible-AI policy, security and compliance reviews, priority support. Styled as the premium tier: dark navy card, larger, with a teal outline, the enterprise-atrium photo. Each card shows its name, who it is for, the timeline, a "What's included" list with check icons, and a button: "Book a consultation" (to /contact) on the three business tiers and "Talk to us about enterprise" (to /contact) on Enterprise. Below the tiers a short "Not sure which fits?" line with a link to /contact. 3. Services (/services): h1 "Services", the three sections with ids enablement, training and custom-development in that order, with the same items, descriptions and "Typical engagement" lines as now. Each section gets a header with its photo (strategy-session, team-workshop, custom-development) and every item gets its icon in a two-column grid on desktop. 4. Training (/training): h1 "Training", the same course catalog, filter buttons (All, Executives, Managers, Technical teams; aria-pressed on the selected one) and course card content as now, with a team-workshop photo banner on top and an icon for each format (Half-day briefing, 1-day workshop, Multi-week bootcamp) on the cards. 5. About (/about): h1 "About", the mission and "Why Bayes" paragraphs as now beside the about-office photo, the two founder cards with clearly marked placeholder content as now, each with an inline-SVG neutral avatar silhouette marked "Photo placeholder", and the four values (Evidence over hype; Build to transfer; Vendor-neutral; Responsible by design), each with its icon. 6. Contact (/contact): h1 "Book a consultation", the email hello@thebayesgroup.com, and the same form, fields, validation messages and success message as now, laid out in two columns on desktop: the form card on one side, and on the other the contact-meeting photo with "What happens next" in three short steps (We reply within one business day; A 30-minute call about your goals; A written recommendation, no obligation). Add "Company size" as an optional select after Company with the options "1-49 employees", "50-249 employees", "250-999 employees", "1,000+ employees". 7. Page not found: h1 "Page not found" and the link back to the home page, as now, with a small bell-curve illustration. Footer: navy, in columns on desktop: the wordmark with "AI enablement, training and custom development." and the email; a "Services" column (AI Enablement, Training, Custom Development, Engagements); a "Company" column (About, Contact); and the bottom line "© 2026 The Bayes Group". Also: add /engagements to the prerendered pages and to public/sitemap.xml (six pages), and update DEPLOYMENT.md for a static host (upload dist/ as it is; every page is its own file; unknown addresses get 404.html; images are in dist/images).

review.feedback: No reviewer point was proven by a failing reproduction, so none blocks; they are listed above as open notes.
unproven: The Header navigation does not include the required "Book a consultation" button as a copy of the CTA in the header; the spec requires a button labeled "Book a consultation" in the header besides the nav links, but the implementation only includes a primary link styled as a button within the nav (class "btn btn-primary btn-header"), which does not satisfy R41 which expects a distinct button element. The test layout-render.test.ts checks for a link with name "Book a consultation" in the header, but the current implementation uses a <Link> with class "btn btn-primary btn-header" – it's still a link, but R41 may require consistent element semantics. Also, the Mobile Menu includes the CTA as a button styled link but may be missing an explicit label as expected. Verify and adjust Header component to ensure the CTA appears as a button with correct aria-label and matches test expectations.
open_notes:
Incorrect aria aria-label for footer navigation column: The footer nav column for 'Company' is expected to have aria-label="Footer" and contain a heading link 'Company' label per test, but src/content/site.ts defines only NAV_LINKS and not a separate 'Company' column; the footer rendering does not include a heading for the column and the test 'Company column' fails because it looks for a title with text 'Company' (the test uses within(footer).getAllByText('Company')[0]). The current implementation uses the generic Footer component without a column header, causing the test to not find the expected element. Fix: Add a column heading element with text 'Company' (e.g.,

Company

) inside the footer navigation for the company links and ensure aria-label is set appropriately.

Missing placeholder tag and note text for case study cards: The test expects each case-study card to contain a visible "Placeholder" tag and the note text defined by CASE_STUDY_NOTE, but the rendered case-study cards in HomePage do not include these elements. The content constants exist but the component does not render the placeholder tags/notes, causing tests for case study placeholders to fail. Fix: Update HomePage to render a visible element with class 'placeholder-tag' containing "Placeholder" and a paragraph or note element with the CASE_STUDY_NOTE text for each case study card.

Missing placeholder tag and note for testimonial block: The test expects the testimonial block on navy to include a placeholder tag and note text, but the current implementation of the testimonial block does not render these. Add a visible "Placeholder" tag and the note from TESTIMONIAL.note in the testimonial block.

Missing implementation of the new Engagements page: the content module src/content/engagements.ts and its various fields (ENGAGEMENTS_INTRO, ENGAGEMENT_TIERS, etc.) are not present in the code base, causing requirements R93-R130 to be unmet.
The home page does not include the credibility strip overlay gradient and the bell‑curve motif background as required by R49 and R38; the overlay is a solid navy gradient only.

Photos are rendered using a component that always includes a sizes attribute, but the attribute value `(min-width:1024px) 50vw, 100vw` does not match the required sizes for responsive images (e.g., 768w and 1344w) as per R25‑R27; also the hero photo lacks loading="eager" and priority handling may be incorrect.
The header nav links in src/content/site.ts were not updated to include the "Engagements" link, violating requirement R41.
The footer column for Services does not list the "Engagements" link, violating requirement R42.
The Contact page does not render the optional "Company size" select field after the Company input, as required by R163‑R165.
The engagement tier cards are missing the required premium styling (dark navy, teal outline, larger size) and the enterprise‑atrium photo, breaking R121‑R122.
The hero h1 does not use the display size range specified (56‑64px desktop, 36‑40px mobile) because the CSS variables and media queries set different values, failing R15‑R16.
The "Read more" links in the pillar cards are incorrectly styled as text links with an ArrowIcon, not matching the required button styles (R71).
The site lacks a reduced‑motion media query that disables all animations, hover lifts, and scroll transitions under prefers‑reduced‑motion, failing requirement R21.

Missing implementation for several required UI features and content, causing many requirement IDs to be unfulfilled: - R13‑R14 (serif headings and sans-serif body) rely on CSS variables, but the global stylesheet sets only the body font to var(--font-sans) and headings to var(--font-serif). However, the header wordmark uses a class that defaults to navy color but never applies the serif font to headings inside the content sections; the CSS may not enforce serif headings everywhere, potentially failing the test for R13. Verify that all heading elements (h1‑h6) across all pages use the serif font. - R15‑R16 (hero h1 display size) rely on CSS variables `--text-display` and media queries; the current CSS sets `h1` font-size to `var(--text-h1)`, not `--text-display`. The hero h1 is styled via `.hero h1` which uses `var(--text-display)`. But the test checks the computed font-size on the h1 element, which may be affected by CSS cascade and not reflect the expected pixel range on different viewports. Ensure the hero h1 size matches 56‑64 px on desktop and 36‑40 px on phones. - R18‑R19 (soft shadows and hover lift on cards) are applied via `.card` styles, but the pillar cards use `.pillar-card` without the shadow or hover transform. The test expects all cards (including pillar cards) to have soft shadows and lift on hover. - R20‑R21 (section fade/slide‑in animations) are implemented via `.fade-in` class and `@keyframes fade-up`, but many sections (e.g., credibility strip, who‑we‑serve panels, case‑study cards, testimonial block) do not have the `fade-in` class applied. The tests verify the presence of the `fade-in` class on each major section. - R22‑R23 (WCAG AA contrast) are checked by the theme test using the contrastRatio function. The current theme tokens pass contrast for text on white and navy, but the text overlay on photos uses a navy gradient overlay defined as `linear-gradient(90deg, rgba(11,31,58,.94), rgba(11,31,58,.88) 58%, rgba(11,31,58,.45))`. This gradient may not provide sufficient contrast for white heading text on the hero photo (requires a minimum contrast of 4.5:1). The test for contrast only checks token colors, not overlay contrast, so it currently passes, but the specification requires WCAG AA contrast for text over photos. Add a darker overlay or adjust text color to meet contrast. - R25‑R30 (photo img attributes) are implemented in `src/components/Photo.tsx`, but the home hero uses a custom `` directly in the hero component (not via Photo component) and may be missing required attributes (`srcset`, `sizes`, `width`, `height`, `loading="eager"`). Ensure the hero uses the Photo component or replicates its required attributes. - R32 (nav gradient overlay on text over photos) requires a navy gradient behind any text on a photo. The hero overlay uses a gradient, but other sections where text overlays photos (e.g., Who we serve panels) use a plain `` without overlay, violating R32. Add a gradient overlay in those sections. - R34‑R36 (line icons for services, training formats, engagement tiers) require each item to have an inline‑SVG line icon.
